answer_summary: π–π stacking energies between two layers of one COF-8 repeat unit (kJ mol^-1): AA = -85.7 (1 eclipsed t-t + 10 eclipsed b-b contacts); AB = -75.6 (6 slipped b-b contacts, triazine nodes above hexagon-hole centres); AB' = -333.6 (6 slipped b-t contacts, complementary hole-centred registry). Values are computed from the problem's own interaction table (-7.9/-12.6 b-b, -49.8/-55.6 b-t, -6.7/-16.7 t-t) counting only aromatic units (triazine cores and benzene/phenylene rings; vinyl C=C and nitrile units excluded per the problem's assumption).
assumptions: Repeat unit of one COF-8 layer contains 1 triazine ring and 10 benzene/phenylene rings carrying pi density (read off the printed COF-8 structure with the blue dashed repeat-unit boundary).
Vinyl C=C linkers and nitrile groups are not aromatic and contribute no pi-pi stacking, per the problem's explicit assumption.
AA registry = perfectly eclipsed: 1 t-t + 10 b-b eclipsed contacts per bilayer repeat unit.
AB registry = triazine nodes above hexagon-hole centres: 6 slipped b-b contacts (edge-midpoint aromatic jobs over benzene jobs), no t-t contacts.
AB' = complementary hole-centred registry: 6 slipped b-t contacts; AB and AB' are inequivalent because no lattice translation swaps the up-/down-pointing edge-midpoint triangles.
The given AA' datum (-67.1 kJ/mol) is an independent problem input and was not used to calibrate any of the three requested outputs.
Interaction energies are additive over ring-ring contacts using the two table columns (eclipsed vs slipped) as printed.
source_gaps: The ring-contact multiplicities (10 b-b eclipsed for AA; 6 b-b slipped for AB; 6 b-t slipped for AB') are distilled from the printed structure and stacking-mode figures and asserted as definitions in the Lean file; the problem supplies these only pictorially, so a machine-checked derivation of the multiplicities from a formal honeycomb geometry is not possible from the provided inputs alone. All arithmetic consequences of the counts are formally proved with only standard Lean axioms.
